chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar al-Sabati who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with two divorces for the waiting period, then she married for a temporary marriage (mut'ah). Is she permissible for her first husband after that? He said, 'No, until she marries permanently (batatan).'

key_terms.بَتَاتًا: Permanently / in a single permanent contract

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a husband to remarry his wife after she has had two divorces and a temporary marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific condition for a woman divorced twice to return to her first husband, requiring a genuine, permanent marriage (*batatan*) rather than a temporary one (*mutah*). This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence to ensure the *khula'* (third marriage) is not merely a formalistic arrangement to facilitate remarriage. The ruling underscores the integrity of the marital bond as a prerequisite for the finality of the triple divorce.
